labor.named_not_headcount: ORNL checklist names grading contractor, construction contractor, landscape contractor; AF&PA names job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector — not a headcount

labor_notes: Do not invent crew counts. ORNL names grading / construction / landscape contractors. AF&PA names job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring) not in these books — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods.
habit_scope: 1–2 story light-wood SFR / ADU. ORNL Fig 1-4 foundation-type decision + HUD R401.4 soils + HUD §3.9 floodplain local. Not 3-story, not MF, not steel.
how_it_is_done: Decide foundation type before documents: basement, crawl, or slab-on-grade (ORNL Fig 1-4). Then construction system (concrete / masonry / wood), then details (insulation, structural, drainage/waterproof, termite, radon), then finalize construction documents and establish QC inspection procedures (ORNL Fig 1-4 last box).

Read the site: topography, water table, presence of radon, soil type, depth of bedrock (ORNL §1.3 Site Conditions). Any type can sit on a flat site. A slope often means walkout basement or crawl. Water table within ~8 ft of the surface makes a basement undesirable — drainage/pumping usually cannot be justified (ORNL §1.3).

Climate/frost is part of the type pick: a deep frost already forces a wall, so basement incremental cost is smaller in the north; Gulf Coast needs no frost footing (ORNL §1.3). Wasatch/Logan frost-depth basement habit and Fontana slab habit are MarketNotes (mn-wasatch, mn-logan, mn-fontana), not a new number from this pass.

Order the hole that tells you the dirt: ORNL SITEWORK 'Call for test hole (full depth hole in proposed foundation location)' and 'Confirm elevation of water table'. That order is P00; the digging of the test hole is P01.

HUD §4.3 / IRC as printed: soil-bearing investigations rarely required for residential except known risks (organic deposits, landfills, expansive soils, seismic). Table 4.2 / IRC table R401.4.1 presumptive values only when the codes do not require geotechnical investigation reports (IRC section R401.4). SPT (ASTM D1586) 'usually are not warranted for typical residential applications' (HUD §4.3). Do not invent a geotech on every lot.

Floodplain: local zoning and/or building codes govern any construction in a floodplain (HUD §3.9). Basic premise: elevate above expected flood or build outside the regulatory floodplain. Full floodplain regulations are beyond HUD RSDG scope. BFE usually the 1-percent annual exceedance; community may add freeboard. FIRM from FEMA Map Service Center. Lowest living floor / foundation type / materials below BFE are named as governed — not a how-to from this book.
Delivery method (custom vs spec vs ADU) is not in ORNL / HUD RSDG / AF&PA. Gap. Do not invent a delivery SOP.
Expansive clay or bedrock near the surface: ORNL §1.3 names special techniques / piles to stable strata — Constraint c-P05-piles-not-inland-habit, not a new Method from this set.

common_messups: Picking a basement on a water table within ~8 ft (ORNL §1.3 veto).
Inventing a geotech on every SFR lot when HUD says investigations are rarely required except known risks (HUD §4.3).
Treating floodplain as a national HUD how-to — HUD says local zoning governs (HUD §3.9).
smart_save: HUD §4.3: SPT instrumentation and cost usually not warranted for typical residential; presumptive table R401.4.1 when R401.4 does not require a report. No dollars in sources.
do_not_cheap: Test hole at the proposed foundation location (ORNL SITEWORK).
Geotech when R401.4 requires it or known risks (organic, landfill, expansive, seismic) (HUD §4.3).
Floodplain: local zoning / BFE path — do not skip because HUD did not reprint the ordinance (HUD §3.9).
Foundation type before permit drawings (ORNL Fig 1-4; later P05 methods are permit-gate).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit: decide type and order reports before dirt. Not an alt.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping the test hole / water table on a wet lot (ORNL). Using a basement against the ~8 ft water-table veto. Inventing delivery-method or HOA steps from silence.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — superintendents pick basement vs slab from frost and water table. What they skip is writing the Fig 1-4 path (termite + radon details + QC inspection procedures) into the documents before permit.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Foundation type and any floodplain elevation/foundation restriction belong on drawings. Engineer when R401.4 requires investigation or tables fail. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
risk_if_swapped_late: Changing basement vs slab vs crawl after this decision is a type change: excavation depth, waterproofing, drain tile, floor package, stairs. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Before anyone moves dirt, decide what the house sits on. Wet high water table kills a basement. Frost already puts a wall in the ground in the north so a basement is the usual buy. Order a full-depth test hole at the house location. Most SFR lots do not need a fancy geotech — HUD says the code table is enough unless the lot is a known problem or the code demands a report. Floodplain is local zoning, not a HUD cookbook. Custom vs spec vs ADU is not in these books.
spanish_summary: Antes de mover tierra, decida sobre qué se sienta la casa. Nivel freático alto mata el sótano. En el norte la helada ya pide pared, así que el sótano es lo habitual. Pida un pozo de prueba a la profundidad de la cimentación. HUD dice que la mayoría de lotes SFR no necesitan geotecnia cara — la tabla del código basta salvo riesgo conocido. La llanura de inundación es zonificación local. Custom vs spec vs ADU no está en estos libros.
